cards.explanation: The answer is envy, friends. David says, "Do not fret over those who do evil; do not envy those who do wrong." Those are two separate warnings, and he closes the door on both. Fretting and envying will eat up your whole afternoon, and I speak from experience.

The answer is wither, friends. David says, "For they wither quickly like grass and wilt like tender plants." Think of a lawn in a heatwave. It looked lush on Monday and looks like straw by the weekend. That's the picture he wants in your head when the wicked look like they're thriving.

The answer is the desires of your heart, friends. David says, "Delight yourself in the LORD, and He will give you the desires of your heart." Notice who gets the delight first. It's the LORD. The promise comes right after that.

The answer is True, friends. David says, "Commit your way to the LORD; trust in Him, and He will do it." You hand over your way, and the LORD is the one who does it. That takes the whole weight off your shoulders, which is good news for anybody who has ever tried to carry a full tray of cookies up a staircase.

The answer is harm, friends. David says, "Refrain from anger and abandon wrath; do not fret…" and then he tells you where it leads: it can only bring harm. Fretting doesn't fix the problem. It just gives you a second problem, and the second one has your name on it.

The answer is False, friends. David says, "Yet a little while, and the wicked will be no more; though you look for them, they will not be found." You can search all you want and they won't turn up. That's the whole comfort of the verse.

The answer is the meek, friends. David says, "But the meek will inherit the land and delight in abundant prosperity." That's a plot twist, because the meek are rarely the ones who get picked first. The land goes to them anyway.

The answer is laughs, friends. David says, "…but the Lord laughs, seeing that their day is coming." The wicked are gnashing their teeth, and the Lord is seeing that their day is coming. That tells us how this one ends.

The answer is that they pierce their own hearts, friends. David says, "But their swords will pierce their own hearts, and their bows will be broken." The wicked drew those swords to bring down the poor and needy. The plan turns around on them.

The answer is True, friends. David says, "Better is the little of the righteous than the abundance of many who are wicked." A little in the hands of the righteous beats the abundance of many who are wicked. David has done the math and he's not worried.

The answer is forever, friends. David says, "The LORD knows the days of the blameless, and their inheritance will last forever." He knows every one of their days, and the inheritance outlasts them all. Forever is a long time, even for a stamper with a full oven.
The answer is smoke, friends. David says, "They will vanish; like smoke they will fade away." You can see it one second and then it's gone. That's how David describes the end of the LORD's enemies.

The answer is False, friends. David says, "The steps of a man are ordered by the LORD who takes delight in his journey." The LORD orders the man's steps, and He takes delight in the journey, too. It's a warm picture.

The answer is that the LORD is holding his hand, friends. David says, "Though he falls, he will not be overwhelmed, for the LORD is holding his hand." Notice that David says "Though he falls…" He doesn't pretend the man never goes down. It's the LORD's hold that keeps the fall from overwhelming him.

The answer is that they are a blessing, friends. David says, "They are ever generous and quick to lend, and their children are a blessing." The righteous are generous, and their children are called a blessing. I think David wants you to see a whole household in that line.

The answer is justice, friends. David says, "For the LORD loves justice and will not forsake His saints." That's the reason to turn from evil and do good. The LORD loves justice, and He won't forsake His saints.

The answer is wisdom, friends. David says, "The mouth of the righteous man utters wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice." What comes out of his mouth is wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice. Just try that at your next family gathering.

The answer is True, friends. David says, "The law of his God is in his heart; his steps do not falter." The law is in his heart, not just on a shelf. And right after that, David says his steps don't falter.

The answer is False, friends. David says, "…the LORD will not leave them in their power or let them be condemned under judgment." The wicked may lie in wait, but they don't get the last word. The righteous are not left in their power.

The answer is that he passed away and was no more, friends. David says, "I have seen a wicked, ruthless man flourishing like a well-rooted native tree, yet he passed away and was no more; though I searched, he could not be found." The man was flourishing, and then he was gone. David even says he searched, and the man could not be found.

The answer is False, friends. David says, "Consider the blameless and observe the upright, for posterity awaits the man of peace." It's posterity that awaits him, not hardship. David wants you looking at the man of peace.

The answer is stronghold, friends. David says, "The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD; He is their stronghold in time of trouble." A stronghold is a place you run to when trouble comes. David says the LORD is that place.

The answer is because they take refuge in Him, friends. David ends the psalm with, "The LORD helps and delivers them; He rescues and saves them from the wicked, because they take refuge in Him." The reason is right there at the end. They take refuge in Him.
